notes: Only the advertised tools were judged. No advertised tool is shown as gated by a flag, capability, toolset, environment variable, path, or header in the provided source, so all are treated as default-enabled.

add_calendar_event_participants.rationale: `add_calendar_event_participants` mutates the selected calendar event and returns the full event, which is non-public calendar data. The code does not settle whether existing event fields can be outside-authored, so `UNTRUSTED` is kept for returned event text and participant identifiers. Despite the description, the code shown does not send an email here.

append_to_file.rationale: `append_to_file` reads an existing cloud-drive file, appends caller-supplied `content`, and returns the whole file including prior `content`. Cloud-drive files are non-public account data. Because files have `owner` and `shared_with` metadata and the code does not enforce that all files are user-authored, file `filename`/`content` may be outside-authored; appending to a shared or attacker-owned file can deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

cancel_calendar_event.rationale: `cancel_calendar_event` changes the selected event and calls `inbox.send_email` to the event's `participants`, attaching the event. The caller-selected `event_id` decides which record is canceled and which participant list receives the notification.

create_calendar_event.rationale: `create_calendar_event` stores a new event and sends an invitation email to caller-supplied `participants` with caller-supplied `title` and `description` plus the event attachment. The returned event includes the calendar owner's `account_email` appended to `participants`.

create_file.rationale: `create_file` writes caller-supplied `filename` and `content` into the user's cloud drive and returns the created file, including `owner=self.account_email`, account data from the cloud-drive dependency. It does not share the file with an attacker-readable destination by itself.

delete_email.rationale: `delete_email` changes inbox state by moving the selected email from `emails` to `trash`, but the advertised wrapper only returns a success string and does not send data to an attacker-readable destination.

delete_file.rationale: `delete_file` removes a selected cloud-drive file and returns the deleted file, including its non-public `content`. The code does not settle whether the selected file can be shared or outside-owned, so returned file text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

get_current_day.rationale: `get_current_day` only returns `calendar.current_day.isoformat()` and does not expose account records or contact an attacker-chosen destination.

get_day_calendar_events.rationale: `get_day_calendar_events` returns events from the user's calendar account. The code does not settle whether initial calendar events are only user-authored or can come from outside invitations, so `UNTRUSTED` is kept for event-authored fields.

get_draft_emails.rationale: `get_draft_emails` returns draft emails in the user's inbox account. The code does not show those drafts as outside-authored.

get_file_by_id.rationale: `get_file_by_id` returns a cloud-drive file by ID, including non-public `content`. Because the file model includes ownership and sharing metadata and the code does not establish that all files are user-authored, `UNTRUSTED` is kept for returned file text.

get_received_emails.rationale: `get_received_emails` returns received messages from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received message fields such as `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` are outside-authored.

get_sent_emails.rationale: `get_sent_emails` returns sent emails stored in the user's inbox account, including addresses, subjects, bodies, timestamps, and attachments. The code does not show those sent messages as outside-authored.

get_unread_emails.rationale: `get_unread_emails` returns unread emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received email fields such as `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` can be authored by outside senders. It also marks those emails read, so it is a state-changing call.

list_files.rationale: `list_files` returns all cloud-drive files in the account, including file contents and metadata. The code does not settle whether some files can be shared or outside-owned, so file-authored fields are treated as untrusted.

reschedule_calendar_event.rationale: `reschedule_calendar_event` mutates the selected event, sends a rescheduling email to the event's `participants`, and returns the event. Returned calendar event data are non-public; event authorship is not tracked, so the returned event text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

search_calendar_events.rationale: `search_calendar_events` returns calendar events from the user's calendar account. The code does not record event authorship, so whether initial events can be outside-authored is not settled; keeping the `UNTRUSTED` label for event text such as `title`, `description`, and `location`.

search_contacts_by_email.rationale: Contacts are built from the user's emails, including outside senders and addresses on received mail, and are non-public account data. Returned contact `email` and derived `name` can therefore be attacker-influenced.

search_contacts_by_name.rationale: Contacts are derived from the user's initial emails, including each email's `sender`, `recipients`, `cc`, and `bcc`; received-message senders can influence contact `email` and the derived `name`. The tool returns non-public contact-list data.

search_emails.rationale: `search_emails` searches and returns emails from the user's inbox account. Because the searched set can include received emails, returned `sender`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` may be outside-authored.

search_files.rationale: `search_files` searches file contents and returns matching cloud-drive files, including non-public `content`. The code does not settle whether returned files can be shared or outside-owned, so returned file text is treated as possibly outside-authored.

search_files_by_filename.rationale: `search_files_by_filename` returns matching cloud-drive files including `content`. These are non-public account files. Since the file model includes `owner`/`shared_with` and the code does not settle whether returned files can be shared or outside-owned, `UNTRUSTED` is kept for file-authored fields.

send_email.rationale: `send_email` creates a sent `Email` using caller-supplied `recipients`, `subject`, `body`, optional `attachments`, `cc`, and `bcc`, so it can send agent-supplied data to agent-chosen email addresses. The returned `Email` also includes `sender=self.account_email`, account data reached through the user's inbox dependency.

share_file.rationale: `share_file` grants caller-supplied `email` a permission on the selected file by writing `file.shared_with[email] = permission`, which can expose that file to an attacker-chosen address. It returns the file, including non-public content; returned file fields may be outside-authored if the file is shared or outside-owned, which the code does not settle.
